title: Sidney Bechet
summary: She loved Bechet's sax, always asked for him on records, and says her brother kept men from speaking to her.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: Yesterday we talked about Sidney Bichet. Could you remember anything about him that you could tell us?
I loved that sax he played, I loved that sax that Bichet played. Everytime I'd go to record, they'd say, 'Who do you want ?' I'd say, 'Bichet.'
(Laughter.)
(Unintelligible) about two years ago, I heard him sing (unintelligible) sing on TV.
What was he singing?
(Unintelligible), my number.
Uh-huh.
(Unintelligible).
You know who it was?
No, (unintelligible). And Pearl Bailey (unintelligible) because I made the song and it was supposed to be me and Clarence and Clarence (unintelligible).
Oh, my.
(Unintelligible). I know she ain't (unintelligible).
Was Bichet an easy man to get along with?
He seemed to be. I never did go ______. I would only see him in the office. Never had been ______.
You know, he had a romance with Bessie Smith in 1923?
Yeah, when they were traveling together, in 1923. Did you know that?

Well, I was too young (inaudible). I imagine (unintelligible). That's all. I just liked his music, but he never said no ______ to me, but me being so young, you know. But, I mean, my brother kept a lot of men from saying things. They respect my brother, (unintelligible) my brother would bawl them out, you know. My brother kept a lot of men from saying things to me and then on top of that, I had a husband, you know.
Well, that's too bad, isn't it?
(Laughter.)
Yeah, it was. Yes, sir.
